The SD stays around ~2, suggesting substantial lot-level heterogeneity beyond measurement noise. To discriminate between a single broad distribution and two latent populations, I want a compact per-temperature mixture diagnostic using simple 1D clustering on the observed y values; if component means are stable while weights shift with T, that would support the colleague’s hint.
```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

exp_all = pd.concat([exp08, exp10, exp12], ignore_index=True)

def kmeans1d(arr, k=2, iters=50):
    x = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float)
    qs = np.quantile(x, [0.33, 0.67]) if k == 2 else np.quantile(x, np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, k))
    centers = np.array(qs[:k], dtype=float)
    for _ in range(iters):
        d = np.abs(x[:, None] - centers[None, :])
        lab = d.argmin(axis=1)
        new_centers = centers.copy()
        for j in range(k):
            if np.any(lab == j):
                new_centers[j] = x[lab == j].mean()
        if np.allclose(new_centers, centers):
            break
        centers = new_centers
    order = np.argsort(centers)
    remap = np.zeros_like(order)
    remap[order] = np.arange(k)
    lab = remap[lab]
    centers = np.sort(centers)
    return lab, centers

for T, d in exp_all.groupby("T"):
    y = d["y"].to_numpy()
    lab, centers = kmeans1d(y, k=2)
    out = d.copy()
    out["cluster"] = lab
    stats = out.groupby("cluster")["y"].agg(["count", "mean", "std", "min", "max"])
    print(f"\nT={T}")
    print("overall mean/std:", float(out["y"].mean()), float(out["y"].std()))
    print("2-cluster centers:", centers)
    print(stats.to_string())
